question: During a log-roll manoeuvre for a suspected cervical spine injury, the person controlling the head and neck should be positioned at the patient's side (along the torso) and should call the commands for the roll.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is FALSE. The head controller must be at the head end, maintaining in-line neutral traction, and is the leader who calls all movement commands. Three assistants align along the patient's side. Misplacing the head controller is a critical error that risks converting an incomplete SCI into a complete one.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is FALSE. The person controlling the head and neck must kneel at the HEAD END of the patient (not the side). This person is the designated leader who calls all commands ('ready — roll — stop'). Placing the head controller at the side would compromise in-line traction and coordination. The three assistants controlling the torso, pelvis/thighs, and legs are positioned along the side.
